entities.label: Evidence
entities.summary: The Solothurn–Moutier railway line is a 22 kilometre-long standard-gauge line in Switzerland, connecting Solothurn via the Weissenstein Tunnel to Moutier in the Bernese Jura. At the start of operations in 1908, the Emmentalbahn took over operations of the line, which was owned by the Solothurn-Münster-Bahn. In 1997, it merged with the Emmental-Burgdorf-Thun-Bahn (EBT) and the Vereinigte Huttwil-Bahnen —which already worked together for the operation of trains—to form the Regionalverkehr Mittelland (RM), which then took over the operation of the line.
